extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and worked examples for merchant arithmetic: positional multiplication with errors, proportional methods, and many applied word problems (market/trade computations). The text teaches how to manipulate positional quantities, propagate and eliminate 'errors' in digit-positions, and use proportions to recover unknowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication with positional 'errors' (propagation of digit-position errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: When numbers have 'errors' located in particular digit-positions, treat each error as a quantity to be multiplied by the other number(s) in the usual multiplication; the contribution of each error in each position is found by multiplying that error by the other multiplicand and placing the product in the appropriate position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives repeated examples: "quando tu multiplicadi d numero ... il primo errore in la seconda posizione ... vieni a multiplicare li coi numeri ..." — i.e. multiply the first-position error into the second position (and vice versa), compute the individual products, then combine them. Use this to see how an unknown digit's error affects the overall product. Examples show explicit multiplications (e.g., products like 48, 72, etc.) and summation of those products to determine net effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine products from errors across positions to obtain net effect
rubrics_metrics.description: After multiplying each positional error by the counterpart multiplicand, sum the resulting partial products (taking account of positional alignment/carrying) to obtain the total change caused by the errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly demonstrates forming the 'congiunto' (sum) of products of the errors (e.g., "il congionto de li erro2i ... la somma ... fa ...") and compares it to the true product to deduce unknowns. Examples show assembling partial products (like 24, 48, 72, etc.) and summing to reach totals used to resolve the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination/recovery of unknown digits by using differences of positions
rubrics_metrics.description: If certain positions (or their differences) are known but a digit is unknown, operate on differences between positions (subtract/add positional amounts) and multiply errors by these differences to form equations allowing the unknown digit to be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages: "per la via de le differencie ... la questione si puo solvere ... la differenzia de le positioni ..." advise multiplying errors by differences of the positions and arranging proportional relations. The method uses known position-differences and the products of errors to isolate the unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'third' and 'fourth' rules (terza e quarta regola) — successive add/subtract operations to reach solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply rules of successive addition and subtraction (repeatedly adding or removing quantities) to change the configuration until the desired relation or known terms are obtained; repeated application can increase or decrease counts to create solvable proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text discusses "la terza e quarta regola ebe in substantia vanno quando piu e meno si giungna" and demonstrates through examples how repeatedly adding or subtracting certain terms leads to configurations from which the unknown can be derived. It emphasizes procedural repetition and checking via examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric demonstration as a justification for arithmetic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where helpful, give a geometric demonstration ('geometrica dimonstratio') to justify the arithmetic manipulations, showing equivalence between geometric area/figure arguments and the algebraic handling of positional products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explicitly mentions providing a geometric demonstration ("geometrica or dimonstratio") as an alternative justification and uses line/area diagrams implicitly to illustrate why rules about multiplication and positional contributions work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate merchant word problems into positional quantities and apply arithmetic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Model story problems (buying/selling, market prices, packing, shares of goods, rates, wages) by assigning quantities to positions/letters (a, b, c, d, etc.), then apply the positional multiplication and difference rules to compute totals, proportions, and unknowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous applied examples: buying grain, paying with coins, counting animals, dividing goods, valuing items at market prices. The guidance shows step-by-step translation: place quantities in positions, note which are known/unknown, perform multiplications/divisions, and use the above rules to find answers (examples include computed totals like 120, 200, 240, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve proportional problems by converting to known-term proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: When terms are proportional or can be put into proportional relation, convert the problem into proportional terms (using known 'termini noti') and continue proportionally to recover unknown terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text advises 'operare per via de termini noti ... numeri proportionali' and gives examples of continuing proportional sequences until the unknown is found. This mirrors the rule-of-three style reasoning common in mercantile arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repeated multiplication and combination to handle composite multiplicands
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiplicand is composite (e.g., made of several parts or repeated units), multiply each part separately by the multiplicand(s), then combine the results to obtain the total product; repeated application yields the final sum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show splitting multiplicands and multiplying piecewise ("multiplicando ... per ... venne ... poi ..."), then summing partial results (e.g., multiplications leading to 48, 72, 20, 56, etc.) and assembling them into the final total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for carries and place-value alignment when summing partial products
rubrics_metrics.description: When summing partial products produced by positional-error multiplications, properly align by place value and carry over digits as necessary to reflect true decimal/positional structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the examples the author aligns partial products in 'positione prima' and 'positione seconda' and notes when carry/overflow occurs (implicit in the arithmetic examples where sums like 48+24 etc. produce higher-place contributions). The method relies on correct positional alignment to deduce unknowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer worked illustrative examples for each rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For each procedural rule, present concrete numerical examples (market and counting problems) that demonstrate the rule's application end-to-end so the learner can follow and verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter is full of worked examples (buying/selling, counting animals, doubling/halving, converting units). The text repeatedly states and then exemplifies the rule: 'fia la vera solutione ... e noi ... la dimostramo ... con linee' — i.e., state rule, then show examples and numerical computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize problem-solving by placing known quantities in named positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up problems by designating line/position labels (a, b, c, d, etc.) for known and unknown quantities; use those labels consistently through the manipulations to derive relations and compute unknowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly refers to 'linea a b', 'numero a b c d', 'prima posizione', 'seconda posizione' and instructs taking quantities 'per la prima posizione' or 'per la seconda posizione' — this structural labeling is central to following the algorithms and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use practical unit-conversion and valuation techniques for trade computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply unit conversions, per-unit pricing, and bundle/pack valuations (e.g., value per balla, per capo, per gallina) using multiplication/division and the above positional/proportional rules to compute totals or per-item prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several merchant problems: converting sacks to smaller units, valuing bales or pieces at market, computing what is paid given partial payments, and distributing goods. Examples show the method: express quantities in consistent units, multiply by unit price or divide to distribute, and use proportional arithmetic to complete the computation.
